gates: identity determinism and revisions; FIFO/dedup/queue-full retry; zero-budget; partial real packaging; bounded work; LRU eviction/retry; leases and publication pinning; resident admission; cancellation queued/running/waiting; actual builder cancellation; failure/factory/oversize; yielding work retained; stale queue/cache/lease; independent actual source gate; actual revised rebuild; exact cell/RGB/roles vs prior frozen oracle
scope: Isolated single-owner cooperative CPU admission/cache prototype around unchanged frozen root+interaction builders. No threads/native/Assets integration.
accounting: Owned artifact exact array element payload is17bytes per stored cell: Int3+uint tint+byte role. Row30 context is retained with None role; owned rendering/collision remains below30.
Accounted artifact bytes add512bytes plus twice identity-string character counts as an explicit envelope allowance; this is not exact CLR heap measurement.

A single active job reserves24MiB throughout root construction, interaction classification and incremental packaging, including waiting publication. Shared immutable templates/context and terrain-provider storage are caller-owned and excluded.
The resident ledger includes pinned/retired entries plus the worker reservation. Artifact publication transfers accounting from worker to cache.

Work units count supplied job candidates plus a unit for bounded controller start/publication/failure handling. Those metadata units may scan/evict up to configured64 ready entries; they are not millisecond guarantees.

Third-party IJob producers are trusted cooperative callbacks: reservations and Step work reports are checked but cannot sandbox arbitrary allocations, exceptions or CPU time. The included adapter uses the independently bounded frozen builders.
production_wiring: Create immutable shared template/context after pack load; snapshot terrain revision and original pose into Identity.For.
Keep this controller on one coordinator-owned execution lane. Request returns QueueFull explicitly; retain the placement request outside and retry when capacity changes. Do not silently discard it.

Pump bounded candidate budgets from the chosen worker/coordinator. Cancel tickets and invalidate source/context revisions on travel, regeneration or unload. Frozen builders independently reject changed terrain identity.

Acquire a lease only after publication. Build/upload render meshes and collision/resistance data from the same complete cell+role payload, with row30 context excluded from ownership. That downstream mesh/collider transaction is not implemented here.
Release leases after consumers finish. A completed worker waiting for pinned capacity remains pending; caller must release/cancel/backpressure deliberately.
Provider identities must never be reused after mutation. Recheck before downstream upload/publication; a cached CPU snapshot does not certify current GPU or gameplay state.
limitations: No asynchronous worker, Unity scheduler, native meshes, colliders, GPU buffers, actual memory-residency measurements or frame-time guarantees.
No disk persistence, cross-session cache, global cache or production generator/version change.

This controller bounds its own records and declared accounting, not caller-retained terminal tickets, provider data, shared templates/context, CLR garbage collection backlog or arbitrary producer allocations.

Identity/current-provider callbacks must be side-effect-free. Pump explicitly rejects producer reentry; trusted callbacks and cooperative byte/work reporting remain API contracts. Lease reads reject stale/current mismatches; lifecycle still requires caller release.
Only the two recorded actual redwood fixtures and focused controller cases were exercised; no live travel/Play validation.
